## p210 A1, p210 A2 — p210 A — Helsinki and return transport for the Ostsee Division

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p210-a-p210-a--helsinki-and-return-transport-for-the-ostsee-division"></a>


[Source certificate](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/certificates.json)

**Record:** the two parts of p210 A, intercepted on 20 November 1918.
**Result:** all **208 plaintext positions** are fixed from **416 source
coordinates** under the published Nov19–21 key. Four explicit coordinate
substitutions give the following readable reconstruction.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p210-a-reading"></a>

### Reading

**Readable German:**

> Fustation Helsingfors mitteilet hierher, ob Ruecktransportmoeglichkeit
> fuer Ostseedivision gesichert.
>
> Andernfalls wird versucht, Schiffe dorthin zu entsenden. Welcher
> Verladehafen kaeme in Frage? Zentralfunkleitung, Vollzugsrat Berlin.

**Meaning:** The radio station at Helsingfors is asked to report whether
return transport for the Ostsee Division is secured. If it is not, the
sender will try to send ships there and asks which embarkation port would
be suitable. The closing names the Central Radio Direction and the
Executive Council in Berlin.

The unusual **MITTEILET** is retained as a same-length reading; it is not
silently shortened or replaced with a longer modern expression. The names
Helsingfors, Ostseedivision and Berlin are directly deciphered. The source
does not establish whether the proposed shipping was subsequently arranged.
Word spacing, punctuation and capitalization are editorial.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p210-a-two-source-frames-and-exact-costs"></a>


## p210 B — End of Consul Burkhardt's oil-company assignment

**Edition context:** p210 B — Consul Burkhardt's oil-company assignment.

<a id="edition-cases-people-p210-b-p210-b--consul-burkhardts-oil-company-assignment"></a>


[Source certificate](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/certificates.json)

**Record:** p210 B, 20 November 1918, to Consul Burkhardt in Tiflis.
**Result:** **158/158 raw plaintext positions** are fixed by the unchanged
published Nov19–21 key. Five explicit coordinate substitutions restore
body words; the date-like **J** and the administrative references remain
literal and historically unresolved.

<a id="edition-cases-people-p210-b-readable-body"></a>

### Readable body

**Readable German:**

> An Konsul Burkhardt, Tiflis. Ihr Auftrag fuer
> Kriegsschmieroelgesellschaft am J Dezember beendet.
> K.R.A. Nr. 455, JJ, J4, A. Nch.
> Kriegsministerium, Allgem. Kriegsdepartement.

**Meaning:** A War Ministry telegram informs Consul Burkhardt in Tiflis
that his assignment for the lubricating oil company is ended on a December
date. Its day is transmitted as **J** under the published key. This edition
does not silently turn that letter into a numeral or establish a specific
historical completion date.

The addressee and place are directly read. `KRA`, `A NCH`, **455**, **JJ**
and **J4** remain source strings without a forced administrative expansion
or date interpretation. The prose supplies only spacing, capitalization
and punctuation. It does not identify the consul beyond the printed surname.

<a id="edition-cases-people-p210-b-raw-text-and-reconstruction-cost"></a>

`KRIEGSSCH1IEROELGESE8LJCHAFT → KRIEGSSCHMIEROELGESELLSCHAFT`.
The exact coordinate substitutions are:

| Source index, zero-based | Source | Proposed |

## p210 C — Fuller inquiry about NCO Kurt Richter in Aleppo

**Edition context:** p203 C / p210 C — inquiries about Richter in Aleppo.

**Related source pages:** [p203 C](203.md#source-p203-c).

<a id="edition-cases-people-richter-aleppo-p203-c--p210-c--inquiries-about-richter-in-aleppo"></a>


[Source certificate](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/certificates.json)

**Records:** two related personnel inquiries, on 18 and 20 November 1918,
under different published period keys. **Result:** the earlier message
fixes **93 of 96 raw positions** without any source edit. The later fixes
**201 of 204**, and its readable body requires six coordinate substitutions
and three source-erasure fills. Their postal-number fields differ; they
are not forced into one recovered number.

<a id="edition-cases-people-richter-aleppo-the-earlier-inquiry-p203-c"></a>

### The earlier inquiry, p203 C

**Readable German:**

> K.M., Abt. Nachrichtenmittel, erbittet Nachricht Verbleib Untffz.
> Richter, Funkerpark Aleppo, Feldpost ???.

**Meaning:** The War Ministry's communications-equipment section asks
for news of the whereabouts of an NCO named Richter at the radio park
in Aleppo. Its field-post number remains unresolved.

The source abbreviation **UNTFFZ** is retained. Its interpretation as an
NCO is supported by the later message's directly read **UNTEROFFZ**.
The earlier message itself does not supply the first name Kurt.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
KMXABTXNACHRICHTENMITTELXERBITTETNACHRICHTVERBLEIBUNTFFZXRICHTERXFUNKERPARKXALEPPOXFELDPOSTX???X
```

</details>

All **192** coordinates in [p203 C](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p203_C.png)
are valid and unchanged. The three question marks are unknown square-cell
values, not damaged source glyphs. The source section belongs to the
**18 November** heading, below an earlier 16 November section:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
XYZ v LP (03.51 p.m., November 18th)
IWE KOW AS FUER XYZ 14.50 (18/11)
RICHI-192
```

</details>

<a id="edition-cases-people-richter-aleppo-the-later-inquiry-p210-c"></a>

### The later inquiry, p210 C

The same-length editorial reconstruction reads:

**Readable German:**

> Ist ueber den Unteroffz. Kurt Richter, Aleppo, Armeenachrichtenpark
> J527, Deutsche Feldpost 227, Auskunft ueber jetzigen Standort oder
> Verbleib zu erfahren? [Raw following character: J.]
> Nr. Q90 strich JJ, J4, A. Nch. Kriegsminist., Allgem.
> Kriegsdepartement.

**Meaning:** The later message asks whether information can be obtained
about the current location or whereabouts of NCO Kurt Richter in Aleppo,
giving an Army Signals Park designation and field-post number. The name
**KURT RICHTER**, Aleppo, and **FELDPOST227** are directly read.
The designation **J527**, references **Q90 / JJ / J4**, and the isolated
`J` following `ERFAHREN` remain literal. They are not silently converted to
numerals or a reconstructed reference.

The [p210 C source](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p210_C.png)
has **408** coordinate slots and this header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
XYZ v LP (02.55 p.m., November 20th)
17.40 (20/11)
RICHI-408
```

</details>

Its raw decipherment under the unchanged Nov19–21 key is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
IS0XEBERDENUNTEROFFZXKURTXRICHTERXALEPPOXARMEENACHRICHTENPARKXJ527XDEUTSCLEFELDPOSTX227XAUSKUNFTUEBER3ETZIGENSTANDORTOWERVERBLEIBZUERFAHRENJXNRXQ90STRICHJJXJ4XAXNCHX?RIEGSMINISTXALLGEMXK?I?GSDEPARTEMENTXX
```

</details>

The invalid source glyphs in **AFEVF**, **CXVVA** and **EGFDF** retain
their positions in the literal transcript. For analysis, they are masked
as erasures at source indices **302, 365 and 385**. The candidate fills
those slots with **F, G and F**, respectively. The remaining body repairs
change six valid coordinates:

| Source index, zero-based | Source | Proposed |
|---:|:---:|:---:|
| 50 | G | X |
| 61 | G | F |
| 230 | A | X |
| 265 | A | X |
| 316 | G | F |
| 378 | X | V |

These give the readable opening `IST UEBER`, `DEUTSCHE`, `JETZIGEN`,
`ODER` and the War Ministry closing. The candidate preserves **399 valid
source coordinates** and re-encrypts exactly after the six changes and
three fills. It adds no plaintext letters and does not change the key.
The question mark in the spaced German is editorial punctuation; the
following literal `J` is explicitly acknowledged above.

<a id="edition-cases-people-richter-aleppo-why-the-postal-number-is-not-transferred-across-keys"></a>

### Why the postal number is not transferred across keys

The shared surname, rank and Aleppo location support reading these as
related inquiries. They do not establish that the address fields were
identical or copied without error.

| Message and positions | Printed-key result | Observed pairs |
|---|---|---|
| p203 C, 92–94 | `???` | `VA VA VV` under Nov16–18 |
| p210 C, 84–86 | `227` | `DG DG DA` under Nov19–21 |

The earlier first two digits are one shared unknown, and the last digit
must be different under an injective square. The base domain for each
cell is `{0,3,4,5,6,7,8,9}`. The later **227** cannot simply be copied back:
that would put `2` at **VA**, while the unchanged Nov16–18 square already
puts `2` at **DV**. The coordinate certificate checks this conflict.

The separate [p201/p206 order-date inference](201.md#edition-cases-military-p201-p206-orders)
conditionally assigns **VA=5**. If accepted, it would make this earlier
field `55?`; it would not settle the mismatch with `227`. This edition
preserves the evidence without selecting a changed address, a copying
error, or a different digit labelling as the explanation.

## p210 D — Request for a report on the situation in Reval

**Edition context:** p210 D — request for the situation in Reval.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p210-d-p210-d--request-for-the-situation-in-reval"></a>


[Source certificate](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/certificates.json)

**Record:** p210 D, 20 November 1918. **Result:** all **58 plaintext
positions** are fixed from **116 unchanged source coordinates** under the
published Nov19–21 key. One explicitly costed spelling repair gives:

**Readable German:**

> Bitte um Mitteilung, wie Lage in Reval. Kriegsministerium Berlin.

**Meaning:** The War Ministry in Berlin asks for a report on the situation
in Reval. The telegram gives no further description of the situation.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p210-d-source-and-one-repair"></a>

### Source and one repair

The [source image](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p210_D.png)
preserves the header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
KOW v LP (05.55 p.m., November 20th)
FUER RVA 22.00 (20/11)
RICHI-116
```

</details>

Its final groups are **`XXDDV V`**. An earlier OCR reading had an extra
terminal `V` and an uncertain glyph; both are corrected by reading the
source, with no historical-coordinate deletion or invented fill.

The literal decipherment is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BITTEUMMITTEILUNCXWIELAGEINXREVALXKRIEGSMINISTERIUMBERLINX
```

</details>

The proposed **MITTEILUNC → MITTEILUNG** changes source index **6: A→G**.
The other **115** coordinates are unchanged. The candidate retains the
telegram's abbreviated grammar and re-encrypts exactly after that single
substitution. Spacing, capitalization and punctuation are editorial.
